name: Banku with Grilled Tilapia
summary: Tangy fermented corn and cassava dough served with spice-rubbed grilled tilapia and a fiery fresh pepper sauce.
story: Banku is a smooth, slightly sour dough of fermented corn and cassava, popular in southern Ghana. Paired with grilled tilapia and a raw pepper sauce called shito or pepper, it is a favourite at restaurants and weekend gatherings.

items.name: fermented corn dough
items.note: fresh or from an African grocer

steps.title: Marinate the fish
steps.text: Blend the onion, ginger, garlic, lime juice and salt to a paste. Rub it inside the fish and into the slashes and marinate for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Grind the pepper sauce
steps.text: Pound or blend the tomatoes, onion, scotch bonnet, ginger and salt coarsely, so it is chunky and not smooth. Set aside.

steps.title: Grill the fish
steps.text: Brush fish with oil and grill over medium coals or under a hot grill for 8-10 minutes per side, until the skin is crisp and charred in places and the flesh flakes at the thickest part.

steps.title: Mix the banku dough
steps.text: Whisk the corn dough, cassava dough, salt and water in a pot until completely smooth with no lumps. The mixture will look like a thin batter.

steps.title: Cook the batter
steps.text: Cook over medium heat, stirring continually with a wooden spoon, for 10 minutes until the batter thickens into a heavy, sticky mass.

steps.title: Steam and stir
steps.text: Reduce heat, add a splash of water, cover and steam for 5 minutes. Stir and press vigorously against the pot side for 5 minutes until stretchy, glossy and smooth.

steps.title: Shape the balls
steps.text: Wet a bowl, scoop a portion of banku into it and rotate to form a smooth ball, or shape with a wet spoon. Wrap in cling film or leaves to keep warm.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Plate the banku with a whole fish and a generous spoonful of pepper sauce. Eat with your right hand, pinching off banku and dipping.

tips: Lumps are the enemy; whisk the raw dough smooth before cooking.
Keep stirring during cooking or the base scorches.
Slash the fish deeply so the marinade reaches the flesh and it cooks evenly.
Banku is eaten fresh and firms up as it cools.

swaps.swap: Mix fine cornmeal with a spoon of plain yogurt and water, rest overnight; it approximates the sourness.
